SECTION ONE
Purpose, Scope, Basis, Definitions
ARTICLE 1- (1) The purpose of this Directive is to determine the principles of the Industrial Applications
course, which undergraduate students at Gebze Technical University may participate in for a semester in
private sector, public institutions, organizations, and affiliated businesses related to their studies, to enhance
their competitive power and contribute to university-industry collaboration.
ARTICLE 2 - (1) This Directive covers the principles of the Industrial Applications course conducted at
Gebze Technical University.
ARTICLE 3- (1) This Directive is prepared based on the Law No. 2547 on Higher Education, the Law No.
5510 on Social Insurance and General Health Insurance, the Law No. 3308 on Vocational Education, the Law
No. 4447 on Unemployment Insurance, and the Gebze Technical University Regulation on Undergraduate
Education-Teaching and Exams.
ARTICLE 4- (1) In this Directive, the following terms have the following definitions:
a) University: Gebze Technical University (GTU)
b) Faculty: The faculties offering undergraduate education
c) Course: The "Industrial Applications" course offered by the faculties under various codes
d) Industrial Applications Course Faculty Planning Board (IACFPB): The board that plans the process
and operation of the Industrial Applications course
e) Departmental Coordinator: The Departmental Planning Coordinator
f) Workplace: Private sector, public institutions, organizations, and affiliated businesses
g) Workplace Training Supervisor: The training supervisor designated by the workplace for the student
taking the course
h) Collaboration Agreement: The document signed between the workplace supervisor and the Rectorate
determining the quotas allocated to the University by the workplaces and conditions of the workplaces
participating in the Industrial Applications course implementation
i) Implementation Agreement: The agreement between the student and the workplace regulating their
relationship for the course implementation, signed by the student and the workplace training supervisor
under the supervision of the Coordinator
j) Industrial Applications Course Inspector: An academic qualified to teach who works in collaboration
with the Coordinator to monitor the implementation process of the course Schedule at the workplaces and
check the students' status within the process
SECTION TWO
General Principles, Powers and Responsibilities, Evaluation, Final Provisions
ARTICLE 5- (1) The Industrial Applications course takes place during the spring semester of the education-
teaching year, within the training period specified in the University’s Regulation on Associate Degree and
Bachelor’s Degree Education-Teaching and Exams for students who have completed 200 or more ECTS
credits and have a CGPA of 3.00 or above, or those in the top 20% of their class based on their CGPA,
consisting of a minimum 14 -week period students spend at the workplace where they will perform their
applications.

ARTICLE 6 - (1) The number of students that each workplace will accept, as indicated in the signed
collaboration agreement, is evaluated by the department al coordinator and announced before the registration
week. The student who will take the course selects the workplace together with the Coordinator.
ARTICLE 7- (1) The curriculum for the 4th-year spring semester is prepared with alternatives to apply to
students who register for and those who do not register for the Industrial Applications course. The ECTS load
of the Industrial Applications course is determined by the faculty board based on the recommendations of the
related departments, in accordance with the Regulatory Framework on Applied Trainings in Higher Education.
ARTICLE 8- (1) At the end of the semester, a two -person jury consisting of the department al coordinator
and the course inspector examines the report submitted by the student to the Department al Coordinator’s
Office. The student presents their work at the workplace to the jury. The jury determines the student's grade
based on the student's course report and the evaluation report from the workplace. The workplace training
supervisor’s grade contributes 50% and the jury’s grade contributes 50% in determining the letter grade. The
departmental coordinator sends the determined grade to the related dean’s office.
ARTICLE 9- (1) The course follows the rules below:
a) The student registered in the course is required to comply with the working hours set by the workplace for
a minimum of 14 weeks.
b) The total absence duration by the student, including reports, cannot exceed 10% of the total workdays;
otherwise, the student fails due to absenteeism.
c) There is no leave entitlement for the student during the course. However, with the approval of the
workplace training supervisor and the Departmental Coordinator, the student may be granted leave not
exceeding 7 workdays. The workplace may add this leave to the end of the term.
d) If a student is absent from the workplace for more than three days without permission or excuse, their
Industrial Applications course will be immediately terminated. The situation is reported to the departmental
coordinator by the workplace in a letter. The course grade will be evaluated as NA.
e) If the student is absent during the inspector's visit, a minute will be written. If this situation occurs a
second time, the student is deemed unsuccessful, and the course grade will be NA. Valid excused situations
of the student are reserved.
f) Sporting students representing the University in any competition or event are considered on assigned
leave for those days upon a letter submitted by the University to the workplace. These days do not count
towards absence.
g) If the student leaves the workplace due to compulsory courses in their program or to meet with their
advisor for Graduation Project-II, this does not count as absenteeism.
ARTICLE 10- Obligations of the registered student are as follows:
a) Students are primarily obliged to comply with all the rules and principles set by the workplace during the
implementation period.
b) At the end of the semester, students prepare a report summarizing all activities and knowledge and skills
reinforced during the Industrial Applications course, have it approved by the workplace training supervisor,
and submit it to the Departmental Coordinator in both printed and electronic formats no later than the first
week of the final exam schedule. The student will present and defend the report orally before the department
jury on the last day of the second week of the final exam schedule.

ARTICLE 11- (1) Under the course, students are subject to the provisions of the Disciplinary Regulation for
Students at Higher Education Institutions for any disciplinary issues. They are also required to comply with
the workplace’s disciplinary and occupational health and safety rules.
ARTICLE 12- (1) The Industrial Applications Course Faculty Planning Board (IACFPB) consists of the dean,
vice-dean, rel ated department heads, and department al coordinators. The IACFPB is responsible for
identifying issues related to the course implementation, developing solution proposals, presenting opinions
and recommendations regarding legal or administrative regulations to the Rectorate, and organizing advisory
meetings, when necessary, with the participation of workplace representatives to enhance the effectiveness of
the course's implementation.
ARTICLE 13 - (1) The D epartmental C oordinator is appointed by the r elated department head. He/she
implements the decisions made by the IACFPB and the work program related to the course. He/she ensures
all the communication and coordination necessary for the most successful execution of the course. The
Departmental Coordinator manages the process of selecting workplaces for the course, evaluating student
requests. If he/she deems appropriate, the D epartmental Coordinator can add a workplace to the Industrial
Applications course list, provided that the workplace signs the Industrial Applications Course Protocol with
the University. His/her term is two years, and he/she may be reappointed.
ARTICLE 14- (1) The Course Inspector is a qualified academic staff member appointed upon the proposal
of the Departmental Coordinator and by the department head. The inspector monitors the students registered
in the course by visiting the company at least once every three weeks to evaluate the fitness of the time students
spend in the workplace to the course’s purpose , assess their performance, and help resolve any issues they
may encounter with the workplace.
ARTICLE 15- (1) After the student is placed in the workplace for the In dustrial Applications course, an
implementation agreement is signed within the framework of the collaboration document established with the
workplace, which outlines the obligations of both the workplace and the student. The implementation
agreement comprises of consists of course content designed by the Coordinator with input from the student’s
academic advisor, along with additional clauses, if necessary, based on the workplace's field of activity and
procedures. The agreement is issued in two copies and becomes effective with the approval of the IACFPB.
ARTICLE 16- Workplace’s Obligations:
a) The workplace designates a training supervisor for the student. The training supervisor must hold at
least a bachelor’s degree related to the student’s academic field. During the course, students work under
the supervision of the supervisor assigned by the workplace. The workplace training supervisor’s
responsibilities include:
i) Providing the necessary environment and conditions for the development and reinforcement of
students' knowledge and skills,
ii) Assisting students in maintaining work discipline,
iii) Monitoring the students' work performance and completing an evaluation form at the end of the
period, submitting it to the Coordinator in a sealed envelope.
b) The workplace is expected to provide the student with free access to transportation and other social
services available to employees. However, the workplace is not obliged to grant students access to
financial benefits provided under a legal right or a collective agreement.
c) The workplace may choose to provide a stipend to the student.

d) The workplace training supervisor is responsible for informing students about the workplace (such as its
organizational structure, scope of work, and work environment) before the course period begins.
ARTICLE 17- University’s Obligations:
a) For students registered in the course, the premiums for occupational accidents, occupational diseases, and,
if applicable, general health insurance for those not covered by any social security institution are paid by the
University in accordance with Law No. 5510.
b) The university exercises the student’s financial rights in accordance with the Regulation on the
Procedures and Principles for Covering the Payments to Undergraduate Students in Science and Engineering
Fields Undergoing Mandatory Applied Training from the Unemployment Insurance Fund.
SECTION THREE
Matters Not Covered in the Directive
ARTICLE 18- In cases not covered by this Directive, the provisions of Law No. 2547, the Higher Education
Council, the Interuniversity Council, the Gebze Technical University Regulation on Undergraduate
Education-Teaching, the Senate, the University Executive Board, the Faculty Executive Board, and other
relevant legislation provisions apply.
Enforcement
ARTICLE 19- This Directive comes into effect on the date it is approved by the Gebze Technical University
Senate.
Execution
ARTICLE 20- The provisions of this Directive are executed by the Rector of Gebze Technical University.
